title: Introducing Virtual Models on AI Gateway
description: Today, we are introducing Virtual Models on AI Gateway . Virtual Models are an abstraction of the model string and configurations your apps and developers use. With a single virtual model ID, you can change and update models, configure fallbacks and priority, and enforce Zero Data Retention centrally. The virtual model configuration applies wherever the ID is used. Assign a virtual model ID to an agent task, and pass it as the model string wherever that task is called. You can then change the model and settings behind the virtual model ID in AI Gateway, and your apps and agents will pick up the new configuration automatically, without code changes or redeploys. New models use the same virtual model ID In the last 90 days, 125 new models from more than 10 labs became available on AI Gateway. That adds up to about 10 a week. AI Gateway already makes switching a one-line change. You call any of those models by ID, and AI Gateway routes each request to a healthy provider and can fall back to others when one fails. That one line still lives in your code, so switching usually means a redeploy. Virtual Models move model selection and configuration to AI Gateway. You create an ID for a task, like vmc/coding-agent , and then configure the model and the settings it should use: You can then use that virtual model ID as the model string wherever the task runs: For coding agents like Claude Code , Codex , and others, connect them with vercel ai-gateway setup , then select your virtual model in each harness's model picker or configuration. When a different model is available, including one from another provider, edit the virtual model . Every app and agent that calls vmc/coding-agent picks it up within a few minutes, with no code change or deployment needed: Give each task its own model An agent task like support ticket triage can run hundreds of times an hour and needs to be cheap. Other tasks, like legal contract review, may only run a few times a day, but require a high level of reasoning. You can now give each task a purpose-built virtual model and easily evolve that model and configuration over time: Settings such as fallbacks, Zero Data Retention, and tags stay with the virtual model when you switch models. Provider options apply per provider, so an Anthropic-specific setting stops applying when you point the virtual model at an OpenAI model. Review your provider options whenever you switch providers. Before you switch a virtual model that serves production traffic, point a second one, like vmc/coding-agent-candidate , at the new model and run your evals against it. If quality drops after the switch, point the original back at the previous model. Govern which models your team uses and how Anyone on your team can call a virtual model, and team roles control who can make changes to it. Platform and security teams can centrally govern and test models and settings, while still easily giving teams access to new models as they are released. Settings on a virtual model win over the same settings in a request, so callers can't override the provider order, fallbacks, or service tier you chose. For example, you can configure the fallback models for vmc/storefront-assistant centrally, and every app using that virtual model ID will use the same failover configuration, even if a request specifies different fallbacks. If a virtual model requires Zero Data Retention or providers that don't train on request data, those configurations are enforced even if a request explicitly sets zeroDataRetention or disallowPromptTraining to false. Tags on a virtual model replace any tags sent with the request, so spend lands on the task no matter how each app tags its calls. The Virtual Models page shows requests, spend, and success rate for each task. Get started Create a virtual model from your team dashboard or with the Vercel CLI . About AI Gateway AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and doesn't charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. Virtual Models work with every model type on AI Gateway, including image, video, speech, embedding, and realtime models, and with the AI SDK and the OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs. See the Virtual Models documentation for every setting. Read more

title: Introducing Vercel CI
description: Coding agents are opening more pull requests than ever, and each one waits on CI before anyone can review or merge it. Most CI systems run the entire workflow on every push, even a one-line change. The more your agents push, the more time you spend waiting on CI. Today, we're announcing Vercel CI in Beta. It runs only the tasks affected by your code change, and spins up only the compute those checks need, the same way Fluid compute scales with your traffic. At Vercel, our CI now keeps up with our coding agents. Time from git push to "CI passed" is 2-6x faster than it was before. How it works Vercel CI uses Turborepo to understand your tasks and which ones depend on each other. It reads turbo.json , so if you're already using Turborepo, there's no separate CI config to write. If you're not on Turborepo yet, add turbo.json and the turbo package. It works in single-package repos too. Then tag the tasks you want Vercel CI to run. "tags": ["ci"] is all you need to get started. No workflow YAML to maintain, no drift between your CI config and turbo.json , and Remote Cache is on by default. When you or your agent push code, Vercel CI determines which tasks need to run based on the change. Tasks whose inputs haven't changed come from cache. The remaining tasks each run on their own machine, powered by Hive , Vercel's compute layer, and start as soon as their dependencies finish. Vercel CI gives each task the compute it needs and nothing more. Running your CI on Vercel To get started, follow the documentation or prompt your agent from your repo: Once set up, you or your agent can watch and inspect CI through the Vercel dashboard , Vercel CLI , or Vercel MCP . When something fails, go straight to the failing task, see what's blocked behind it, and open its logs, or search across recent runs to see whether a test has been flaky all week. Vercel CI posts a check to your pull request on GitHub, so your existing branch protection rules can block merges on failure, the same way they do today. Closing the loop Vercel CI has already completed nearly 8 million tasks across our own repositories and the private beta, and we're just getting started. We're working to keep shrinking the time between writing code and running it in production. As we work toward general availability, we plan to add: Advanced observability A vc ci CLI command for distributed execution before pushing code More granular test selection Vercel CI is available in Beta today on all plans. Read the docs and try it on your repository. Read more

title: Vercel Agent can now validate alerts before paging
description: Vercel Agent can now investigate alerts from Vercel monitors before they reach your paging system. With validation enabled for a webhook destination, only alerts Agent classifies as Critical are sent to it. To enable validation: Open a monitor’s notification settings and create or link a webhook destination for your paging system, such as incident.io. Select Critical Only next to that destination. You can also configure notification destinations with the Vercel CLI using vercel monitors notifications . Add --critical-only when linking or updating a webhook destination. Agent checks logs and metrics to assess impact. For example, it can identify health-check errors that don’t affect customers or confirm sustained 5xx errors affecting checkout requests. You can also add context to each monitor to guide Agent’s investigation. Alert validation is available on Pro and Enterprise plans with Observability Plus. Observability Plus includes ten Agent investigations per billing cycle, with additional investigations billed separately . Custom monitors cost $0.0035 per GB of data scanned. Built-in alerts remain included with Observability Plus. Learn more in the alert webhook documentation . Read more

title: Virtual models now available on AI Gateway
description: Virtual models are now available on AI Gateway . A virtual model is a saved configuration that tells AI Gateway which model and settings to use. Your apps and agents call it with a custom model ID, such as vmc/coding-agent . You can change the model or settings centrally in AI Gateway without redeploying your apps or reconfiguring your agents. Use virtual models to: Configure coding agents: Set reasoning effort, fast mode, prompt caching, and other options even when your agent doesn’t expose them. Control routing and compliance: Choose providers, configure fallback models, and enforce requirements such as Zero Data Retention . Attribute spend: Attach custom reporting tags to every request that uses the virtual model. To create a virtual model, open the Virtual Models page and click Create Virtual Model . Enter a slug, choose the underlying model, configure the settings you want requests to use, and save. Or create one with the Vercel CLI : To use a virtual model, replace the provider model ID in your AI SDK or compatible API requests with vmc/<slug> , such as vmc/coding-agent . For coding agents , connect to AI Gateway with vercel ai-gateway setup if needed, then select your virtual model in the agent’s model picker or configuration. Virtual models work with every model type on AI Gateway. Read the launch post for examples or learn more in the virtual models documentation . Read more

title: Run Paseo agents on Vercel Sandbox
description: Paseo now supports running fx, Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, and Pi in the cloud with the Vercel Sandbox plugin . You can now start an agent in Vercel Sandbox from Paseo on your laptop, then connect from your phone to control the same session, even when your laptop is closed. Stopping a sandbox saves your files and conversation history so you can pick up where you left off. Active processes stop with the sandbox. Enter your Vercel AI Gateway key once during setup. The plugin reuses it for model requests across your sessions, keeping the key outside the sandbox. To get started, enable plugins in Settings → Plugins in Paseo. Then install the plugin: Learn more in the Sandbox documentation , Paseo plugin listing , and the Paseo related projects documentation . Read more

title: Particle-1 is now available on AI Gateway
description: Particle-1 from Particle AI is now available on AI Gateway . It is post-trained on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, with a focus on completing software engineering tasks using fewer tokens. Particle describes the gains as shorter reasoning, fewer rounds of trial and repair, and more focused exploration. Set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY in your environment.
